Name: Aloevera
Description: A succulent plant species known for its medicinal properties. It is cultivated worldwide for its gel, which is used in various health and beauty products.
Location: Found in tropical climates, commonly grown in gardens and as potted plants indoors.
Medical_Usage: Used for treating skin conditions, burns, wounds, and as a dietary supplement.

Name: Amla
Description: Also known as Indian gooseberry, it is a deciduous tree known for its edible fruit rich in vitamin C.
Location: Native to India and grows in tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used in Ayurveda to boost immunity, improve digestion, and enhance hair health.

Name: Amruthaballi
Description: Also known as Guduchi or Tinospora cordifolia, it is a climbing shrub valued in traditional medicine.
Location: Found throughout India, particularly in tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to enhance immunity, treat fever, and manage diabetes.

Name: Arali
Description: Commonly known as Oleander, it is an evergreen shrub or small tree with toxic properties.
Location: Native to the Mediterranean region and Asia, often used as an ornamental plant.
Medical_Usage: Despite its toxicity, it has been used in traditional medicine for heart conditions; however, its use is not recommended without medical supervision.

Name: Astma_weed
Description: Also known as Parthenium hysterophorus, it is an invasive weed known to cause respiratory issues.
Location: Native to the Americas but has spread to many tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Generally considered a harmful weed; contact can cause skin irritation and respiratory problems.

Name: Badipala
Description: Known as Clerodendrum serratum, it is a shrub used in traditional medicine.
Location: Found in India and Southeast Asia, typically in forests and hilly regions.
Medical_Usage: Used in Ayurveda for respiratory disorders, inflammation, and as an expectorant.

Name: Balloon_Vine
Description: Also known as Cardiospermum halicacabum, it is a climbing plant with balloon-like fruits.
Location: Found in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used for rheumatism, skin diseases, and respiratory ailments.

Name: Bamboo
Description: A group of evergreen perennial flowering plants in the grass family.
Location: Widely distributed in Asia, Africa, and the Americas.
Medical_Usage: Young shoots are edible; extracts are used in traditional medicine for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

Name: Beans
Description: Seeds of various genera of the flowering plant family Fabaceae, used as vegetables for human or animal food.
Location: Cultivated worldwide in suitable climates.
Medical_Usage: Rich in protein, fiber, and vitamins; beneficial for heart health and diabetes management.

Name: Betel
Description: A vine whose leaves are commonly chewed with areca nut in many Asian cultures.
Location: Native to South and Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for its stimulant effects and to treat bad breath and digestive issues.

Name: Bhrami
Description: Also known as Bacopa monnieri, it is a creeping herb used in traditional medicine.
Location: Found in wetlands across Asia, Australia, and the Americas.
Medical_Usage: Used to enhance cognitive function, reduce anxiety, and improve memory.

Name: Bringaraja
Description: Known as Eclipta prostrata, it is a herbaceous plant used in traditional medicine.
Location: Found in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Used for liver disorders, skin diseases, and promoting hair growth.

Name: Caricature
Description: Also known as Graptophyllum pictum, it is an ornamental shrub with variegated leaves.
Location: Native to New Guinea and cultivated in tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used for treating hemorrhoids, wounds, and skin infections.

Name: Castor
Description: Known as Ricinus communis, it is a fast-growing perennial shrub.
Location: Native to the southeastern Mediterranean Basin, Eastern Africa, and India.
Medical_Usage: Castor oil extracted from seeds is used as a laxative and in skin care products.

Name: Catharanthus
Description: Also known as Madagascar periwinkle, it is a flowering plant with medicinal properties.
Location: Native to Madagascar but cultivated worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Source of alkaloids used in chemotherapy for leukemia and other cancers.

Name: Chakte
Description: Also known as Chakte Viga, it is a tropical hardwood tree valued for its vibrant orange to golden brown wood.
Location: Native to tropical areas of Mexico and Central America.
Medical_Usage: Primarily used for its durable wood in fine furniture, flooring, and turnery; no significant medicinal uses are documented.

Name: Chilly
Description: Commonly known as chili pepper, it is the fruit of plants from the genus Capsicum, widely used as a spice.
Location: Cultivated worldwide, with origins in the Americas.
Medical_Usage: Contains capsaicin, which is used for pain relief and has anti-inflammatory properties.

Name: Citron lime (herelikai)
Description: A large fragrant citrus fruit with a thick rind, known for its aromatic properties.
Location: Grown in tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for digestive issues and as a source of vitamin C.

Name: Coffee
Description: A brewed drink prepared from roasted coffee beans, which are the seeds of berries from the Coffea plant.
Location: Native to tropical Africa, now cultivated in over 70 countries.
Medical_Usage: Contains caffeine, which acts as a central nervous system stimulant; associated with various health benefits and risks.

Name: Common rue(naagdalli)
Description: A herbaceous plant known for its strong aroma and bitter taste, used as a culinary and medicinal herb.
Location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula, now grown worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used to treat digestive problems and as an anti-inflammatory agent.

Name: Coriender
Description: Also known as coriander, it is an annual herb with edible leaves and seeds, used as a spice and garnish.
Location: Native to regions spanning from Southern Europe and Northern Africa to Southwestern Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used to aid digestion and has antimicrobial properties.

Name: Curry
Description: Refers to the curry tree (Murraya koenigii), whose leaves are used as a seasoning in Indian cooking.
Location: Native to India and Sri Lanka.
Medical_Usage: Leaves are used in traditional medicine for their antioxidant properties and to control diabetes.

Name: Doddpathre
Description: Also known as Indian borage or Cuban oregano, it is a succulent herb used in traditional medicine.
Location: Native to Southern and Eastern Africa, widely cultivated in India.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat respiratory issues, digestive problems, and skin conditions.

Name: Drumstick
Description: Also known as Moringa oleifera, it is a fast-growing tree with highly nutritious leaves, pods, and seeds.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent, now grown in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Used for its antioxidant properties, to reduce inflammation, and to lower blood sugar levels.

Name: Ekka
Description: Commonly known as Calotropis gigantea or crown flower, it is a large shrub with milky latex.
Location: Native to South Asia and Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for treating digestive disorders, respiratory issues, and skin diseases.

Name: Eucalyptus
Description: A diverse genus of flowering trees and shrubs, known for their aromatic leaves.
Location: Native to Australia, with some species found in adjacent areas.
Medical_Usage: Eucalyptus oil is used for its antimicrobial properties and to relieve cold symptoms.

Name: Ganigale
Description: Also known as Vitex negundo or Chinese chaste tree, it is a large aromatic shrub.
Location: Native to tropical Eastern and Southern Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for its anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antimicrobial properties.

Name: Ganike
Description: Also known as Lantana camara, it is a flowering plant considered invasive in many regions.
Location: Native to the American tropics, now widespread in tropical and subtropical areas.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for treating respiratory infections and skin conditions.

Name: Gasagase
Description: Commonly known as poppy seeds, derived from the opium poppy plant.
Location: Cultivated in various countries, including India, Turkey, and Czech Republic.
Medical_Usage: Used as a source of dietary fiber and minerals; also has mild sedative properties.

Name: Ginger
Description: A flowering plant whose rhizome, known as ginger root, is widely used as a spice and in medicine.
Location: Native to Southeast Asia, now cultivated in many tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat nausea, digestive issues, and as an anti-inflammatory agent.

Name: Globe Amarnath
Description: Also known as Gomphrena globosa, it is an annual plant with vibrant, globe-shaped flowers.
Location: Native to Central America but widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used for its antioxidant properties and to treat respiratory ailments.

Name: Guava
Description: Psidium guajava is a tropical fruit-bearing tree known for its sweet and aromatic fruits.
Location: Native to Mexico, Central America, and northern South America; now cultivated in many tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to support blood sugar control, cardiovascular health, and digestive health.

Name: Henna
Description: Lawsonia inermis is a flowering plant whose leaves are used to produce a natural dye.
Location: Native to North Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used for its antimicrobial properties and to treat skin conditions.

Name: Hibiscus
Description: Hibiscus rosa-sinensis is a tropical shrub known for its large, colorful flowers.
Location: Native to East Asia but widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used for its anti-inflammatory properties and to promote wound healing.

Name: Honge
Description: Pongamia pinnata, commonly known as the Indian beech tree, is a fast-growing tree with medicinal properties.
Location: Native to India and Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used for its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.

Name: Insulin
Description: Costus igneus, commonly known as the insulin plant, is a medicinal herb believed to help regulate blood sugar levels.
Location: Native to Southeast Asia and widely cultivated in India.
Medical_Usage: Used to manage diabetes; however, it may have side effects such as upset stomach and low blood sugar levels.

Name: Jackfruit
Description: Artocarpus heterophyllus is a tropical tree that produces large, edible fruits known for their distinctive sweet flavor.
Location: Native to South and Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Rich in nutrients and antioxidants; supports digestive health and may have antimicrobial properties.

Name: Jasmine
Description: Jasminum officinale is a flowering plant known for its fragrant white flowers.
Location: Native to the Caucasus, northern Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, the Himalayas, Tajikistan, India, Nepal, and western China.
Medical_Usage: Used in aromatherapy to reduce stress and improve mood.

Name: Kambajala
Description: Kambajala is locally known in parts of South India and is identified as *Hygrophila auriculata*, a medicinal plant commonly found in wetlands and marshy areas.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent; commonly found in moist and marshy environments.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used in Ayurveda for treating liver disorders, jaundice, inflammation, and urinary problems. It has diuretic and hepatoprotective properties.

Name: Kasambruga
Description: Known as Cassia occidentalis, it is a flowering plant used in traditional medicine.
Location: Found in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used for its laxative properties and to treat liver disorders.

Name: Kohlrabi
Description: Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes is a biennial vegetable known for its edible stem.
Location: Cultivated worldwide in temperate climates.
Medical_Usage: Rich in vitamins and fiber; supports digestive health.

Name: Lantana
Description: Lantana camara is a flowering plant known for its colorful blooms.
Location: Native to the American tropics; now widespread in tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used for its antimicrobial properties and to treat respiratory infections.

Name: Lemon
Description: Citrus limon is a small evergreen tree known for its yellow, acidic fruits.
Location: Native to South Asia; now cultivated worldwide in suitable climates.
Medical_Usage: Rich in vitamin C; supports immune function and aids digestion.

Name: Lemongrass
Description: Cymbopogon citratus is a tropical grass known for its lemon-scented leaves.
Location: Native to South Asia and Southeast Asia; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to relieve digestive issues and reduce inflammation.

Name: Malabar_Nut
Description: Justicia adhatoda is a medicinal plant known for its use in treating respiratory conditions.
Location: Native to Asia; commonly found in India and Sri Lanka.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat asthma, bronchitis, and other respiratory ailments.

Name: Malabar_Spinach
Description: Basella alba is a fast-growing, soft-stemmed vine known for its edible, fleshy leaves and stems.
Location: Native to tropical Asia and Africa; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Rich in vitamins A and C, iron, and calcium; supports eye health and boosts the immune system.

Name: Mango
Description: Mangifera indica is a tropical fruit-bearing tree known for its sweet, juicy fruits.
Location: Native to South Asia; now cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Rich in vitamins A and C, fiber, and antioxidants; supports eye health, digestion, and immune function.

Name: Marigold
Description: Calendula officinalis is a flowering plant known for its bright orange or yellow flowers.
Location: Native to southwestern Asia, western Europe, and the Mediterranean; widely cultivated as an ornamental plant.
Medical_Usage: Used for its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties; aids in wound healing and skin conditions.

Name: Mint
Description: Mentha is a genus of aromatic herbs known for their refreshing flavor and fragrance.
Location: Native to Europe, Africa, and Asia; widely cultivated worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Used to relieve indigestion, improve brain function, and alleviate cold symptoms.

Name: Neem
Description: Azadirachta indica is a fast-growing tree known for its medicinal properties.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent; now grown in tropical and semi-tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Has antibacterial, antifungal, and anti-inflammatory properties; used in dental care and skin treatments.

Name: Nelavembu
Description: Andrographis paniculata, commonly known as 'King of Bitters,' is a herbaceous plant used in traditional medicine.
Location: Native to South Asian countries; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat fever, colds, and infections; possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

Name: Nerale
Description: Syzygium cumini, commonly known as Java plum or black plum, is a tropical evergreen tree.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia; cultivated in tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Used to manage diabetes, improve digestion, and boost immunity; rich in antioxidants and vitamins.

Name: Nooni
Description: Morinda citrifolia, commonly known as noni, is a small evergreen tree with distinctive fruit.
Location: Native to Southeast Asia and Australasia; now found in tropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used to boost the immune system, alleviate pain, and improve overall health.

Name: Onion
Description: Allium cepa is a widely cultivated vegetable known for its pungent flavor and culinary uses.
Location: Grown worldwide in temperate climates.
Medical_Usage: Contains antioxidants and compounds with anti-inflammatory properties; supports heart health and immune function.

Name: Padri
Description: Stereospermum chelonoides is a deciduous tree known for its medicinal bark and fragrant flowers.
Location: Native to India and Southeast Asia; found in tropical forests.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine to treat respiratory disorders, fever, and inflammation.

Name: Palak(Spinach)
Description: Spinacia oleracea is a leafy green vegetable known for its high nutritional value.
Location: Native to central and southwestern Asia; cultivated worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Rich in iron, vitamins, and antioxidants; supports eye health, reduces oxidative stress, and improves blood pressure.

Name: Papaya
Description: Carica papaya is a tropical fruit-bearing tree known for its sweet, orange-colored flesh.
Location: Native to Central America and southern Mexico; now cultivated in tropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Contains papain enzyme aiding digestion; rich in vitamins A and C; supports skin health and immune function.

Name: Parijatha
Description: Nyctanthes arbor-tristis, also known as night-flowering jasmine, is a small tree with fragrant flowers.
Location: Native to South Asia; commonly found in India and Nepal.
Medical_Usage: Used in Ayurveda to treat arthritis, fever, and as a laxative; possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

Name: Pea
Description: Pisum sativum is an annual plant producing edible seeds known as peas.
Location: Cultivated worldwide in temperate regions.
Medical_Usage: Rich in protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals; supports digestive health and provides antioxidant benefits.

Name: Pepper
Description: Capsicum annuum, commonly known as pepper, includes varieties like bell peppers and chili peppers, known for their vibrant colors and varying levels of spiciness.
Location: Native to Central and South America; now cultivated worldwide in temperate and tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Capsicum is applied to the skin for arthritis pain and other conditions.

Name: Pomoegranate
Description: Punica granatum is a fruit-bearing shrub known for its nutrient-rich, jewel-like seeds.
Location: Native to the Middle East and South Asia; now cultivated in many regions with a Mediterranean climate.
Medical_Usage: Pomegranates are rich in antioxidants and nutrients, potentially improving heart health, supporting urinary health, aiding in blood sugar control, and offering digestive benefits.

Name: Pumpkin
Description: Cucurbita pepo is a type of winter squash known for its orange flesh and edible seeds.
Location: Believed to have originated in North America; now grown worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Pumpkin is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants; supports eye health, boosts immunity, and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

Name: Raddish
Description: Raphanus sativus is an edible root vegetable known for its crisp texture and peppery flavor.
Location: Believed to have originated in Southeast Asia; now cultivated worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Radishes are low in calories and high in fiber; support digestive health and may have antioxidant properties. [Source]

Name: Rose
Description: Rosa is a genus of flowering plants known for their fragrant and colorful blooms.
Location: Native to various regions across the Northern Hemisphere; cultivated worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Rose water, derived from rose petals, is used for its fragrance and potential skin and health benefits due to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties.

Name: Sampige
Description: Michelia champaca, commonly known as champak, is a flowering tree known for its fragrant yellow or orange blossoms.
Location: Native to South and Southeast Asia; commonly cultivated in tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used in Ayurveda for its potential benefits in treating diabetes, wounds, and cardiac disorders.

Name: Sapota
Description: Manilkara zapota, commonly known as sapodilla, is a tropical evergreen tree producing sweet, brown, kiwi-like fruits.
Location: Native to southern Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean; cultivated in tropical regions.
Medical_Usage: Sapodilla is rich in dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals; supports digestive health and boosts immunity.

Name: Seethaashoka
Description: Saraca asoca, commonly known as the Ashoka tree, is an evergreen tree revered in Indian culture for its beautiful flowers and medicinal properties.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent; found in rainforests and gardens.
Medical_Usage: Traditionally used in Ayurveda for its potential benefits in treating gynecological disorders and promoting reproductive health.

Name: Seethapala
Description: Annona squamosa, commonly known as custard apple or sugar apple, is a tropical fruit-bearing tree.
Location: Native to the Americas; now cultivated in tropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Custard apples are rich in vitamins and minerals; support digestive health, boost immunity, and may have antioxidant properties.

Name: Spinach1
Description: Spinacia oleracea is a leafy green vegetable known for its high nutritional value.
Location: Native to central and southwestern Asia; cultivated worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Spinach is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants; supports eye health, reduces oxidative stress, and may help lower blood pressure levels.

Name: Tamarind
Description: Tamarindus indica is a leguminous tree bearing pod-like fruits with a sweet-sour pulp.
Location: Native to tropical Africa; widely cultivated in South Asia, Mexico, and the Caribbean.
Medical_Usage: Tamarind has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; traditionally used to aid digestion and lower blood sugar levels.

Name: Taro
Description: Colocasia esculenta is a tropical plant grown primarily for its edible starchy corm known as taro root.
Location: Believed to have originated in Southeast Asia; now cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Rich in dietary fiber and essential nutrients; supports digestive health and helps in managing blood sugar levels.

Name: Tecoma
Description: Tecoma stans, also known as Yellow Bells, is a flowering shrub with trumpet-shaped yellow blooms.
Location: Native to the Americas; cultivated in tropical and subtropical climates.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine for managing diabetes and aiding digestive issues.

Name: Thumbe
Description: Leucas aspera, commonly called Thumbe or 'wild basil', is an aromatic plant with medicinal properties.
Location: Native to India; commonly found in open grasslands and along roadsides.
Medical_Usage: Used in traditional medicine to treat cold, cough, and insect bites; possesses antimicrobial properties.

Name: Tomato
Description: Solanum lycopersicum is a commonly cultivated fruit often used as a vegetable in cooking.
Location: Native to western South America; now grown worldwide.
Medical_Usage: Rich in lycopene, vitamin C, and antioxidants; promotes heart health and reduces cancer risk.

Name: Tulsi
Description: Ocimum tenuiflorum, also known as Holy Basil, is a revered herb in Ayurveda.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent; widely cultivated in Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Used for its adaptogenic, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory properties; boosts immunity and relieves stress.

Name: Turmeric
Description: Curcuma longa is a rhizomatous herbaceous plant known for its bright yellow-orange spice.
Location: Native to South Asia; widely cultivated in India and Southeast Asia.
Medical_Usage: Contains curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; used for treating arthritis, digestive issues, and skin conditions.

Name: ashoka
Description: Saraca asoca, known as the Ashoka tree, is a sacred and ornamental tree with clusters of red-yellow flowers.
Location: Native to the Indian subcontinent; often planted in gardens and near temples.
Medical_Usage: Used in Ayurvedic medicine for treating menstrual disorders, uterine problems, and internal bleeding.

Name: camphor
Description: Cinnamomum camphora is a tree known for its aromatic leaves and wood from which camphor is extracted.
Location: Native to East Asia; cultivated in India, China, and Japan.
Medical_Usage: Used in balms and ointments to relieve pain, itching, and congestion; has antifungal and antibacterial properties.

Name: kamakasturi
Description: Ocimum kilimandscharicum, also called camphor basil or Karpooravalli, is an aromatic herb with medicinal value.
Location: Native to East Africa and widely grown in India for its therapeutic uses.
Medical_Usage: Used to treat colds, cough, respiratory issues, and skin ailments; contains natural camphor.

Name: kepala
Description: Cocos nucifera, commonly known as coconut or kepala in some regions, is a tropical palm producing the versatile coconut fruit.
Location: Widely cultivated in tropical coastal regions around the world.
Medical_Usage: Coconut and its derivatives (water, oil) offer antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and hydrating benefits; supports heart, skin, and digestive health.
